links.outcome: Answer quality on AMEGA benchmark with atomic fact-checking versus RAG alone
links.effect: Significant improvement for all LLMs tested (P<.001 for 13/16 models, P<.01 for 2/16, P<.05 for 1/16); human-rated overall answer improvement up to 50% on tumor board cases.
links.quote: The AMEGA auto-evaluation analysis revealed a significant improvement in answer quality by applying our fact-checking algorithm in contrast to RAG only for all LLMs tested ( P <.001 for 13/16 models, P <.01 for 2/16 models, and P <.05 for 1/16 models; Figure 3 ; see Table S6 in Multimedia Appendix 1 ).

links.outcome: Whether post-hoc verification against guideline evidence improves factuality beyond RAG grounding
links.effect: Atomic fact-checking added to RAG improved answer quality; answers improved in 20%, 10%, 50% and 7.7% of cases versus worsened in 8%, 0%, 7.5% and 3%.
links.quote: However, since the proportion of answers that improved (20%, 10%, 50%, and 7.7%) was substantially higher, the overall effect of fact-checking clearly enhanced the answer quality.

links.outcome: Accuracy of tracing each atomic fact to supporting guideline chunk
links.effect: Simple chain-of-thought prompt identified the correct chunk in 75% of cases as first choice and 91.9% among the top 3 chunks.
links.quote: A simple chain-of-thought prompt using GPT-4o identified the correct chunk in 75% of cases as the first choice and in 91.9% of cases among the top 3 chunks, outperforming a complex chain-of-thought prompt (instructing the LLM to assign scores and then rank) and cosine similarity with a text-embedding model (see Figure S4 in Multimedia Appendix 1 and Table S3 in Multimedia Appendix 1 for prompts).

links.outcome: Fact-level verification and source tracing of generated claims against guidelines
links.effect: Framework detected hallucinations (up to 80% detection rate) and traced each atomic fact to source chunks; sensitivity 46-52% on test, tumor board and neurology sets.
links.quote: Additionally, the framework achieved high explainability by tracing each atomic fact back to the most relevant chunks from the database, providing a granular, transparent explanation of the generated responses.

links.outcome: Hallucination and inaccuracy rates in LLM oncology answers, including incorrect dosages
links.effect: Initial RAG answers contained hallucinations and inaccuracies (hallucination rate 0-2%, inaccuracy rate 1-5% of facts); fact-checking detected only 25% of hallucinations in tumor board cases.
links.quote: In the more complex tumor board test set, 25% of hallucinations and 24% of inaccuracies were found, with a balanced accuracy of 72%.
